app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: Envoy (frontend-proxy) routing/config is NOT causing an extra proxy hop or request loop. The observed ~2s latency is dominated by the frontend service handling the /api/shipping request (frontend pod), not by an extra proxy round-trip.
rca_analyses_list.reasoning: Trace 45bc8548ce48ad7d268e4e94a088f46b shows a single Envoy ingress span (spanID ec5ef37259ee13db) and a single Envoy egress/client span (spanID f943f004c4edb419). Both Envoy spans report upstream_cluster=frontend and upstream_address=10.96.115.5:8080 — i.e., Envoy routed directly to the frontend backend. There are no additional Envoy spans pointing to frontend-proxy as an upstream (no evidence of frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend loops). The frontend service’s server span (spanID fbb69d453cd1a324 / GET /api/shipping) has duration ~2.063s, which matches the overall client GET duration (~2.075s, spanID 442443cdadc6dbc0). The frontend-proxy Deployment environment shows FRONTEND_HOST=frontend (deployment description), consistent with correct routing. Together these unique data points rule out a proxy-induced extra hop; the latency is introduced inside the frontend request handling.

final_report.root_cause: The frontend service (pod frontend-559ccb996b-9qp8c) handling GET /api/shipping introduced ~2.06s of processing latency. Trace-level evidence shows the frontend server span (~2.063s) accounts for the full client request (~2.075s); Envoy (frontend-proxy) routing/config was ruled out as the cause (Envoy ingress/egress spans report upstream_cluster=frontend and upstream_address=10.96.115.5:8080 and frontend-proxy Deployment env vars point to frontend:8080). In short: the request is slow because the frontend application’s /api/shipping handler is performing time-consuming work (observed serial downstream calls in the trace to shipping -> quote -> currency) during request processing, not because of an extra proxy hop or Envoy misrouting.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Trace 45bc8548ce48ad7d268e4e94a088f46b shows client GET ~= 2.075s and frontend server span (GET /api/shipping) ~= 2.063s — frontend processing matches observed end-to-end latency. 2) Envoy spans in that trace include a single ingress and a single egress span with upstream_cluster=frontend and upstream_address=10.96.115.5:8080 (no repeated Envoy-to-Envoy hops or loop). 3) frontend-proxy Deployment and pod environment variables include FRONTEND_HOST=frontend and FRONTEND_PORT=8080; frontend Service exposes port 8080 and endpoints at 10.244.1.16:8080 — proxy → frontend routing is consistent. 4) No Envoy response_flags or HTTP error codes indicate proxy/network errors; all spans report 200. 5) frontend-proxy pod has no ConfigMap-mounted Envoy config (configmap not found), but trace evidence shows correct routing to frontend; absence of ConfigMap does not explain the observed client latency. 6) The trace shows serial downstream calls (shipping -> quote -> currency) from the frontend path which explains where frontend CPU/blocking time could accrue.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority 1 (completed): inspected trace 45bc8548... and frontend-proxy Deployment — concluded the large latency is produced inside the frontend service handling /api/shipping, not by an extra Envoy hop or proxy loop. Priority 2 (completed): validated frontend-proxy env vars and frontend Service ports/endpoints — FRONTEND_HOST/PORT match the frontend Service and endpoints. Priority 3 (completed): inspected frontend-proxy env and Service shipping — frontend-proxy pod lacks explicit SHIPPING_HOST/PORT env vars and no Envoy ConfigMap was found, but shipping Service is healthy on 8080; while this raised a possible proxy config gap for shipping, trace evidence still attributes the latency to the frontend server span. No Kubernetes pod/container crashes or network errors were observed. Actions performed: get_trace, multiple kubectl_describe/kubectl_get calls to inspect Deployments, Pods, Services; span correlation to match durations.
